My AI predictions for the next year

1. Fable 5.5 -> Fable 6. GPT 6.1 Astra -> GPT 7

Fable 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Astra will be the last major releases of 2026. I suspect neither will actually ship under those names

Anthropic might even jump straight to Fable 6, just as it did with the unexpected version jump when Fable 5 was released

As for Astra, I doubt it'll be the biggest model in the GPT lineup. OpenAI clearly has something more powerful up its sleeve. My guess is GPT-7 Bel

The end of 2026 will mark the beginning of a transition to an entirely new generation of models

But this is pure speculation

2. 2027 will be the year of radical architectural experimentation

Transformers, at least in their classical form, will gradually give way to more efficient architectural components.

Several major AI labs have already made significant progress in exploring alternatives. The most promising directions include Mamba, Test-Time Training (TTT), and diffusion-based approaches to token generation.

I expect OpenAI and Anthropic to introduce entirely new experimental model families based on this research. They might not even carry the GPT or Claude branding

3. We're going to witness the return of recurrent neural networks (RNNs), which were largely abandoned for years

Promising architectures like RWKV have already demonstrated that modern recurrent approaches have serious potential. In theory, they could also improve training efficiency and quality

4. There will be no RSI miracle.

Recursive self-improvement is a powerful way to automate routine research and engineering tasks, but it still depends on fundamental breakthroughs discovered and implemented by human researchers

And the worse your initial training and RL pipelines are, the greater the risk of regression from recursive synthetic training

It's a similar problem to what we see with distillation

5. New architectures will dramatically reduce the memory requirements of LLMs

Context windows will expand severalfold, while token generation speeds will increase significantly

In 2027, I expect models with context windows of 10 million tokens or more to become increasingly common

6. Haiku- and Luna-tier models will be discontinued

7. We'll see the emergence of highly efficient models with effectively unlimited usage.

It's entirely possible that Anthropic and OpenAI will release models with Opus 5.5-level capabilities that are no longer constrained by weekly usage limits

8. New architectures will revolutionize ultra-small local models capable of running directly on pocket-sized devices.

Major AI labs will develop incredibly efficient on-device models, but instead of releasing them openly, they'll distribute them under restrictive proprietary licenses to a small number of strategic partners, such as Apple, Sony, and others

9. Large open-weight models will fall significantly further behind the closed-source frontier.

Running the most capable open-weight models will still require hardware costing tens of thousands of dollars.

10. DeepSeek will pull even further ahead of its Chinese competitors in 2027

Meanwhile, China's broader AI industry will experience a major downturn. Many labs may shut down or face significant investment cuts as their economic inefficiencies become increasingly apparent

11. Many people predict that the memory and semiconductor shortage will become even worse next year

I'm more optimistic

By mid-2027, I expect a substantial decline in hardware prices and a significant improvement in component availability

12. Google will not win the AI race

Its stock will continue to fall, potentially much further

13. Apple stock will collapse

The company will fail to meaningfully adapt its devices and services to the AI era

Meanwhile, entirely new devices will emerge from smaller, lesser-known companies and AI labs, gradually erasing the boundaries between smartphones, laptops, and servers

Everything will be controlled through a single device, with a substantial portion of the computation happening in the cloud

14. Standalone apps and websites will gradually begin to disappear

Instead of navigating predefined interfaces, users will interact with software generated dynamically in real time for their specific needs

Code itself will cease to be the primary source of value

We're already seeing the first signs of this with ChatGPT and Claude generating interactive widgets directly in their responses. This trend will accelerate dramatically

15. We're about to witness a renaissance in game development

Years of creative stagnation, repetitive formulas, and absurdly bloated development budgets will finally come to an end

Within the next two years, game development costs and production timelines will be cut in half

More and more solo developers will start releasing games with AA+ production quality

Many major publishers will enter a severe crisis. Their stock prices could collapse severalfold

16. 2027 will be the most devastating year for the stock market in human history

We'll witness the decline of an enormous number of corporations that have seemed untouchable for decades

17. Early human trials of a new generation of cancer treatments will demonstrate cure rates approaching 90%

By 2029, these groundbreaking treatments will become widely available

AI GIRLS ARE GETTING HARDER TO SPOT. NOW IMAGINE SELLING THEIR ADULT CONTENT 👀

Look at these two clips. Similar movement, different face, different outfit. The one on the right is AI. Getting that comparison to work is one thing. 

Here’s what I use, step by step. A full guide with the tools and prompts is coming soon in an X article

▹ 1. ChatGPT + Claude = The ideas, prompts and writing
I use both. Sometimes ChatGPT gives me a better prompt, sometimes Claude writes the stronger text. Claude also helps me with video edits. 
First, I work out the character: her appearance, personality, setting and way of speaking. Those details go into a short character sheet I can reuse.
Otherwise, every new post becomes a fresh guessing game. Different face, different personality, different everything - and somehow you’re supposed to build an audience around her. Keep her identity fixed. Change the scene.

▹ 2. Seedream + Nano Banana - Build the look
I use Seedream in Higgsfield to explore the initial appearance, then Nano Banana for targeted edits.
Once I like a face, I save it as the master reference. If the outfit needs changing, I change the outfit. I don’t ask the model to reinvent the whole image.
A useful instruction:
“Keep the character consistent with the reference. Change only the outfit to [description]. Preserve her facial features, hairstyle, pose and lighting.”
Then actually compare the result. Writing “same person” doesn’t guarantee you got the same person.

▹ 3. Soul ID - Make her recognizable beyond one image
In my earlier workflow, I collected 15–20 consistent images before creating a Soul ID. Different angles, expressions and lighting. Same character.
Put the references next to each other. Does it look like one girl’s photo collection, or five girls who happen to have similar hair? Fix that before generating more videos. A convincing image is useful. A character you can keep bringing back is much more useful.

▹ 4. Higgsfield Genjutsu Lite - Transfer the movement
For this comparison, I use Higgsfield Genjutsu Lite to carry the performance into the new version.
Source video, character references, intended changes, then generate and review.
A practical tip from Higgsfield’s guide: use clear movement and references that fit the shot. If the source shows a full body, a close-up of someone’s face leaves a lot for the model to invent. 

▹ 5. Check the awkward frames
The thumbnail looks great. Then she turns around and briefly becomes someone else.
That’s what I check for: face changes, hands crossing the body, hair movement and clothing details that suddenly shift. Also, count rejected generations in your costs. If you generate ten clips and keep two, those two clips have to carry the cost of all ten.
The useful number is cost per publishable clip, not the cheapest price advertised for one generation.

⚠️ Why this needs more than a pretty face
A 2026 meta-analysis covering 210 experiments and 91,058 consumers found no significant overall engagement difference between virtual and human influencers. Virtual influencers generated more novelty, but performed worse on credibility and behavioral intentions. 

My takeaway: getting someone curious isn’t the same as getting them interested enough to become a customer. That research covers influencer marketing, not earnings from AI-companion accounts. But it’s a useful reminder: the reveal gets attention. What comes afterward still has to be good.

▹ 6. JOI Creators - Bring the model you’ve already built
By this point, I already have her face, personality, references and content. I’m not starting over on JOI.

I bring the finished character to JOI Creators, set up her profile, submit her for approval and bring my audience through tracking links. Honestly, this feels like an early-stage gem to me. The appeal is that JOI handles the AI conversations and provides the monetization features. I don’t need to sit in DMs manually replying to every message.

JOI lists subscriptions, video calls, photo/video unlocks, content generation and gifts. Its creator page advertises 80% of revenue from fans who join through your links, with monthly bank or crypto payouts, subject to program terms. Traffic, conversions and earnings are tracked in the dashboard. 

So yes, the interaction and purchase side can run while I’m offline. That’s the passive part - not a promise that money appears without work. I still need to produce content, bring people in and check whether the numbers make sense.

JOI Creators is still in beta. The interface is being refined and will continue improving. The registration link is in my profile and here: https://t.co/Bpwhp5QPEo

That’s my setup: build the model with the tools that work for me, use videos to introduce her, then bring the interested audience to the same character on JOI.

The goal isn’t just a girl people stop scrolling for. It’s a character they remember and come back to.

Neopep: Reinforcement learning from machine-learned force field energy for non-canonical peptide structure prediction

1. Neopep tackles a key bottleneck in peptide therapeutics modeling: non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs) are common in approved peptide drugs, but <0.02% of PDB residues are ncAAs, so standard sequence-to-structure predictors generalize poorly to these chemistries.

2. The core idea is to overcome ncAA data scarcity by adding physics-based supervision: fine-tune a generative structure model using differentiable energy from a machine-learned force field (MLFF), leveraging the fact that native-like conformations are expected to be low-energy under the Boltzmann distribution.

3. Model overview: a sequence-conditioned diffusion model (AF3-style, via the Boltz open-source reimplementation) predicts all-heavy-atom peptide structures for sequences of length 3–50, supporting linear or head-to-tail cyclic peptides. Inputs use Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) atom-level features for ncAAs.

4. Training is two-phase: (i) pretraining on PDB structures (cutoff June 1, 2023) using peptide-length fragments sampled from longer chains to learn a peptide structural prior; (ii) reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning where sampled conformations are scored by a frozen MLFF and the energy signal is backpropagated into the diffusion model.

5. The RL method uses DRaFT-K (Direct Reward Fine-Tuning for diffusion models): only the last K=10 diffusion denoising steps keep gradients for stability and memory efficiency, while the MLFF’s atomic forces are injected as gradients (rather than differentiating through the force field model itself).

6. The energy oracle is SO3LR, a charge-aware equivariant MLFF trained on ~4 million molecular complexes at the PBE0+MBD level. This choice is motivated by MLFFs’ near-quantum accuracy across broad chemistry and better transfer to ncAAs than classical residue-parameterized force fields.

7. A practical enabling contribution is a differentiable hydrogen placement module in PyTorch, extending prior canonical-AA approaches to 189 ncAAs. Since the diffusion model outputs heavy atoms but SO3LR requires all atoms, this module provides differentiable protonation so energy/force signals can train the generator end-to-end.

8. Fine-tuning uses synthetic ncAA peptide generation: sample peptide chains (4–52) from the PDB training set, mutate each position to an ncAA with probability 0.2 (from the 189-residue support), and assign cyclic topology with probability 0.4. No MSAs, templates, or inference-time steering are used in fine-tuning.

9. Evaluation: a new post-2024 PDB test set is curated with MMseqs2 filtering to remove training-like sequences (≥40% identity over ≥80% coverage). It includes 34 ncAA peptides (only those whose ncAAs are supported by the differentiable H placement) and 24 canonical peptides to check for regression.

10. Results (25 samples per peptide, single-sequence mode): Neopep fine-tuned improves ncAA peptide accuracy vs baselines. On non-canonical peptides, mean Min Cα-RMSD is 1.565 Å (vs 2.271 Å pretrained-only, 2.258 Å Protenix-v1 on n=29, 4.448 Å Boltz-2). It also reduces Min heavy-atom RMSD (3.194 Å vs 3.735 Å pretrained-only). Fine-tuning also does not degrade canonical performance and yields competitive/better Min Cα-RMSD (2.211 Å).

15 AI VIDEO CREATION NICHES THAT COULD MAKE YOU MONEY BEFORE THE END OF DECEMBER. 💰

AI is creating new opportunities for creatives, and here are 15 niches I would pay attention to:

1. AI UGC Ads: Create realistic user-generated-style video ads for brands without needing to appear on camera.

2. Product Commercials: Create premium-looking advertisements for physical products.

3. AI Influencer Campaigns: Build campaigns using AI-generated influencers to promote products and services.

4. Beauty & Skincare Campaigns: Create stunning product videos for skincare, makeup and beauty brands.

5. Fashion Campaigns: Produce AI fashion editorials, model showcases and clothing advertisements.

6. Hair Campaigns: Create promotional videos for wig vendors, hair brands and salons.

7. Real Estate Visual Campaigns: Create cinematic property showcases and promotional videos for real estate businesses.

8. AI Spokesperson Videos: Create virtual presenters for businesses, brands and organisations.

9. App & SaaS Commercials: Produce engaging promotional videos for apps, software and digital products.

10. Cinematic Brand Films: Tell compelling visual stories that communicate a brand’s identity and message.

11. AI Micro-Dramas: Create short episodic stories for Facebook, TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.

12. AI Romance & Thriller Stories: Build fictional storytelling channels that can grow an audience and explore monetisation opportunities.

13. AI Music Visuals: Create music videos, visualisers and promotional visuals for musicians.

14. Monthly AI Content Packages: Offer businesses a monthly package of AI-generated reels, promotional videos and social media content.

15. AI Product Photoshoot-to-Video Services: Turn ordinary product images into premium-looking lifestyle videos and advertisements.

Quick advice

Don’t try to learn all 15 niches at once.

Pick one or two, master the creative process, build a portfolio, identify businesses that need the service and start pitching.

You don’t need to wait until you have all the expensive tools. Start with what you can afford, practise consistently and improve your skills.

I won’t pretend to understand the ultimate goal of investing so heavily into making models good at vulnerability research (and not any number of defensive competencies in cyber).

The way model proficiency in VR is being used is primarily to substantiate a view that the models are dangerous, problematic, and in need of regulation.

I could come up with a plausible narrative that has the labs recognizing the ephemeral value of frontier model training (heavy investment for short term returns) and emphasizing the products dangers as a bid towards regulation as a strategic necessity to limit competition. An ok marketer could argue that fearing the product implies how formidable it is (in the short-term).

But that all feels too contrived.

A listener (former exec at a big company I’d often comment on) recently pointed out that despite my best efforts, I still fall prey to the delusion that organizations engage in strategic decision-making when it’s mostly incompetence, intransigence, and whim. 

In response to that apt observation, I’d give more weight to following:

The labs have focused on producing models disproportionately capable at vulnerability research due to a combination of it being (1) easy, (2) high-profile, (3) commercially superfluous, and (4) central to the doomer narrative. 
 
1. Vulnerability research appears easier to RL than the rest of cybersecurity. 

2. VR is a target-rich environment for milestones to publicize. Even if the models hadn’t gotten this good, there’s a wealth of vulns to hype for messaging.

3. VR competency doesn’t yield an immediate product with a quantifiable value (don’t confuse this with the exploit business). So, no comparables or preset price bands. No need for enterprise adoption or organizational diffusion before claiming success. 

4. The competency lends itself to hyperbolic and imaginative myth making about cyber ‘weaponry’ that seemingly validates doomer narratives and tropes (alignment, containment) while gaining fast traction with policy folks and natsec types swayed by militaristic analogies.

I wouldn’t call it an effective strategy because it isn’t one. Hearing that the labs lack the internal coherence to productize anything effectively, byproduct of circumstance seems the more likely origin story.
